chunks: And Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir narrated, saying:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The time for salat enters upon me while I am traveling, so I do not pray until I enter upon my family.” So he said: “Pray and complete the salat.”

I said: “Then the time for salat enters upon me while I am among my family, intending travel, so I do not pray until I depart.” He said: “Pray and shorten, for if you do not do so, then you have opposed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.أَتِمَّ الصَّلَاةَ: perform the salat in complete form
key_terms.أَهْلِي: my family or household at home
key_terms.خَالَفْتَ: you have gone against or opposed
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: being in a state of travel
key_terms.وَ قَصِّرْ: perform the salat in shortened form
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: the prescribed time of salat entering

ai.seo_question: How should salat be performed if prayer time begins before or during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salat during travel based on the state a person is in when the prayer time enters. If the prayer time begins while one is traveling, he prays in full upon reaching home; and if it begins while he is at home intending travel, he prays shortened after departure, in accordance with the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
“I said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as): "The time for prayer enters while I am traveling, so I do not pray until I return home."
Imam (as) said: "Pray and complete the prayer."

I said: "The time for prayer enters while I am at home and I intend to travel, so I do not pray until I have departed."
Imam (as) said: "Pray and shorten the prayer, for if you do not, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah (sw)”.
